page: Microsoft Azure HB120rs_v3 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the HBv3 server family. It is equipped with 120 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel processor and managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features 456.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 3.8 GB of RAM per core.

For storage and connectivity, the HB120rs_v3 includes 2412 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable. The instance is also RDMA (Remote Direct Memory Access) capable, which supports low-latency, high-throughput networking across clusters. No GPU accelerators are present on this configuration.

From a resource density and cost-efficiency perspective, the server provides a high concentration of dedicated compute cores and local NVMe storage, making it structured for parallel computing workloads. The lack of integrated GPUs limits its applicability for hardware-accelerated deep learning, but the combination of 120 dedicated vCPUs, RDMA networking, and local NVMe SSDs supports large-scale distributed simulations, high-performance computing (HPC) tasks, and intensive database operations.
